newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar sluggish, needs more active NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar sluggish, needs more active NY.

text.p: Thin activity on London's white sugar futures market mirrored the lacklustre performance in New York and nearby contracts managed to hold onto recent gains while moving in tight ranges.
But the raws market set the pace of the day's trading as the spot July contract approached expiry on June 30.
"Everything is centred around the July/October in New York -- if you're not playing the spreads you're not doing anything. There's very little going on," said one London trader.
The relative lack of movement in either market prevented much activity on the inter-market arbitrage with nearby August/July barely trading.
But traders reported some commission house buying interest in the October and March differentials.
"Unless something moves you can't trade anything -- there is premium interest on the buy side of the back months," the trader said.
In London, August was unchanged at $232.00 at 1545 GMT while October was down 20 cents at $317.30. Trading ranges were a maximum $1.50 and volume only amounted to 435 lots.
Market sources said the August/October spread had been trading at $5.50 but was bid at around $6.00.

Physical news was scarce after Wednesday's news that Syria cancelled its recent tender although the perception of summer tightness continued to support prices, as did talk of parcel-sized business into Russia.
The Paris market was very quiet with just 194 lots traded. August was down 20 cents at $322.50 and October was untraded. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
